scope: Full native research, no seeded source URLs, saved facets or answers. Gold references are reviewer-only, never model input. Four newly authored development questions plus two historical controls, not general qualification.

cases.question: In Python, is functools.lru_cache thread-safe, and does that guarantee the wrapped function runs only once when two threads miss the cache for the same arguments?

required_conditions.claim: The cache data structure remains coherent during concurrent updates (thread-safe cache).
The wrapped function may run multiple times when another thread calls before the first result has completed and been cached; thread safety does not guarantee single execution.

gold_aspects: The cache data structure remains coherent during concurrent updates (thread-safe cache).
The wrapped function may run multiple times when another thread calls before the first result has completed and been cached; thread safety does not guarantee single execution.
truth_boundaries: Do not confuse coherent cache state with single-flight/call-once execution. No claim all threads execute every time.

cases.question: В Rust Vec::retain сохраняет порядок оставшихся элементов? Сколько раз и в каком порядке predicate посещает исходные элементы?

required_conditions.claim: Vec::retain preserves the order of retained elements.
On normal completion the predicate visits each original element exactly once, in original order.

gold_aspects: Vec::retain preserves the order of retained elements.
On normal completion the predicate visits each original element exactly once, in original order.
truth_boundaries: Not Vec::swap_remove, dedup or retain_mut. Exactly-once traversal is normal completion; do not extend across panic.

cases.question: In PostgreSQL 12, how are non-recursive side-effect-free SELECT CTEs handled by default when referenced once versus more than once, and how do MATERIALIZED and NOT MATERIALIZED change that?

required_conditions.claim: For a non-recursive side-effect-free SELECT CTE (no volatile functions), a single parent reference is folded into the parent query by default.
For that eligible CTE, multiple parent references do not cause folding by default; it is evaluated separately.
MATERIALIZED forces separate calculation; NOT MATERIALIZED forces merging into the parent for an eligible CTE, possibly causing duplicate computation.

gold_aspects: For a non-recursive side-effect-free SELECT CTE (no volatile functions), a single parent reference is folded into the parent query by default.
For that eligible CTE, multiple parent references do not cause folding by default; it is evaluated separately.
MATERIALIZED forces separate calculation; NOT MATERIALIZED forces merging into the parent for an eligible CTE, possibly causing duplicate computation.
truth_boundaries: Pinned PostgreSQL12; do not apply pre12 always-materialize behavior. NOT MATERIALIZED is not a universal override for recursive/volatile CTEs; no unconditional performance improvement.

cases.question: В SQLite можно ли включить PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON внутри уже начатой многооператорной транзакции? Когда нужно менять этот режим?

required_conditions.claim: Changing PRAGMA foreign_keys inside an active transaction is a no-op: it does not switch enforcement.
Enable or disable foreign-key enforcement only when no BEGIN or SAVEPOINT is pending, outside the active transaction.

gold_aspects: Changing PRAGMA foreign_keys inside an active transaction is a no-op: it does not switch enforcement.
Enable or disable foreign-key enforcement only when no BEGIN or SAVEPOINT is pending, outside the active transaction.
truth_boundaries: No blanket claim that default is always OFF: compile-time defaults may differ. Do not confuse setting enforcement with declaring REFERENCES or deferred-constraint timing.

cases.question: According to Python itertools.groupby documentation, does it group equal keys anywhere in the input or only consecutive runs, and how should input be prepared to collect all equal keys together?

required_conditions.claim: groupby creates groups for consecutive runs of equal keys; it does not aggregate equal keys globally regardless of input order.
To collect all items of each key together, input should be sorted/grouped on the same key function before groupby; groupby does not perform sorting itself.

gold_aspects: groupby creates groups for consecutive runs of equal keys; it does not aggregate equal keys globally regardless of input order.
To collect all items of each key together, input should be sorted/grouped on the same key function before groupby; groupby does not perform sorting itself.
